result: Deeper plain networks can train worse than shallower ones (the degradation problem). Letting each block learn a residual F(x) = H(x) − x with an identity shortcut, y = F(x) + x, makes very deep networks trainable: 34-layer ResNet 25.03% vs plain 28.54% top-1 error on ImageNet.
result_plain: Identity shortcuts y = F(x) + x fix the degradation of deep plain nets; deeper ResNets train better.
